title: Known knowns and unknowns
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do you know, what do you know you do not know, and what have you not thought of?

Jose said that the book says in every negotiating session there are different kinds of information: those things we know, like our counterpart's name, their offer and our experience, which are known knowns. Then there is the unknown.
Write what you know, what you know you do not know, and what you have not even thought of.

Jose asked a student to take him to the moment that she switched majors, to visualize where she was. She described being late to her first painting class and the professor's remark that she needs to be on time.
Jose said that when we go to meet a new client, the first thing we do is research on the client.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write your known knowns in the next negotiation.
Write the moment that changed your direction.
Write what you could not have predicted.

choices: Things we know, like their name and offer

check.q: What did Jose say the first step with a new client is?
What did he ask a student to do?
choices: Take him to the moment she switched majors

recap: List what you know, what you do not, and research before you meet.
